reports.entry_comment: Prime 3: Berserker Lords and Berserker Knights

issues.claim: Phazon-based attacks hurt Knights, and late in the crisis the Nova Beam...
issues.problem: This is unclear and partly contradicts both the entry itself and the logbook. The full Knight logbook (now on Metroid Wiki) says: "A Berserker Knight's Phazite armor must be removed before unit can be damaged: only the Phazon-based projectile attacks the creature fires can destroy it." The draft line reads as if any Phazon weapon (for example Hypermode) harms a Knight. That conflicts with the entry's own "can be broken only by the projectiles the Berserker itself fires." The 'Phazon-based attacks' weakness in the infobox refers to the Knight's own reflected shots.
issues.correction: A Knight cannot be harmed at all until its armor is gone. Late in the crisis, the Nova Beam aimed through the X-Ray Visor struck through the plating directly.

issues.problem: The Ship Missile alternative is left out. The Metroid Wiki body says: "Alternatives include firing a Ship Missile at it, or using the Nova Beam to fire through its head." The infobox also lists Ship Missiles as a weakness.
issues.correction: Add a clause: a Ship Missile strike called from her gunship could also bring a Knight down.

issues.claim: Both grades fight with ground shock waves and orbs of Phazon
issues.problem: The Lord's infobox lists 'Shock waves, Phazon Beam'. The Knight's lists 'Shock Waves, Phazon Projectiles' and the body calls them blue projectiles. 'Orbs' is the drafter's own rendering. 'Each Phazon orb' later on overstates it, since Samus did not have to reflect every shot.
issues.correction: Both grades fight with ground shock waves and Phazon projectiles... Samus had to shoot its Phazon projectiles back at it until the plating shattered.

issues.claim: Like the Elite Pirates and the Omega Pirate of Project Helix before them, they are soldiers remade by Phazon.
issues.problem: Project Helix infused Phazon into Space Pirate DNA and embryos (Space Pirate Data). Its Elite Pirates were bred that way, not grown soldiers who were 'remade'. The Berserkers, by contrast, are mutated adult Pirates. Metroid Wiki's Helix-to-Berserker link is itself only a hedged 'it appears'. The sentence also repeats the opening line ('Pirates mutated by Phazon far beyond the regular ranks').
issues.correction: Cut the sentence, or reword it to: "Like the Elite Pirates of Project Helix before them, they are Pirates transformed by Phazon."

issues.problem: These are bare common words. They will fire on ordinary roleplay prose ('fought like a berserker', 'berserker rage') with no Metroid context. The specific keys (Berserker Lord/Knight and their plurals) already cover real uses.
issues.correction: Drop 'Berserker' and 'Berserkers', or move them to secondary_keys with a Pirate/Phazon co-key.

issues.claim: Drafter's note: the Knight logbook was available only in segments
issues.problem: Metroid Wiki now has the full Knight logbook verbatim (quoted above). 'Nearly mindless' and 'a shocking example of the lengths the Space Pirates will go to in their quest for dominance' can be quoted directly if wanted.

reports.entry_comment: Prime 3: Korakk Beast and the Pirate Hussars

issues.claim: A Korakk guards its rider with its life
issues.problem: This comes only from the Metroid Wiki intro ('the Korakk Beasts guard the Hussars with their lives'). The footnote cites the Hussar logbook, which does not say it; the logbook says only that the Korakk avenges a slain rider. The battle section also undercuts it: the Korakk 'will be largely inactive, until the death of its rider'. The entry itself says 'The beast stayed largely passive while its rider fought.'
issues.correction: Delete the clause. Keep the verbatim logbook line: "If a Hussar is slain, his Korakk will fight to avenge his death."

issues.claim: Samus met a lone Hussar, the only one she encountered, mounted on its Korakk
issues.problem: 'A lone Hussar' and 'the only one she encountered' say the same thing.
issues.correction: Samus met the only Hussar she ever encountered, mounted on its Korakk in the Jousting Field of Bryyo Thorn Jungle.

issues.problem: Space Pirate Data does not mention the Korakk, the Hussar or the Jousting Field (I checked). The drafter's note admits nothing in the entry rests on it. Listing it suggests support that does not exist.

Optional context: the fight starts after Samus defeats a pair of Aerotroopers, when the Korakk charges in carrying its Hussar. The Metroid Wiki gallery also shows Samus using the Grapple Lasso on the tail, which ties to the logbook's tail-nerve line.
issues.correction: Optionally: "After Samus downed a pair of Aerotroopers, the Korakk charged into the Jousting Field with its Hussar."

issues.problem: These are real-world words (historical light cavalry) and could trigger in non-Metroid roleplay. The risk is low in this lorebook.
issues.correction: Keep 'Pirate Hussar(s)' and consider dropping the bare 'Hussar(s)' or moving them to secondary keys.

reports.entry_comment: Prime 3: Defense Drone (Elysian guardian of the Boost Ball)

issues.claim: Unlike the Elysians bound to Pirate service, it showed no sign of Phazon corruption, which suggests the Space Pirates never reached the room; it attacked Samus all the same.
issues.problem: The inference is wiki speculation ('Considering the Defense Drone wasn't corrupted or destroyed, the room may not have been explored by Space Pirates'), which canon scope excludes. Calling it 'suggests' does not fix that. It is also undercut by sources the lorebook already uses. Metroid Wiki's Steamlord page, and the existing 'Creatures: Fauna of Elysia and the Pirate Homeworld' entry, both place a Phazon-corrupted Steamlord in Ballista Storage on Samus's return. So corruption did reach that room.
issues.correction: Delete the clause. At most keep: "It showed no sign of Phazon corruption, yet it attacked Samus all the same." Even that observation rests only on wiki commentary.

issues.claim: With Ghor and Helios, the Defense Drone was one of the three great guardians Samus faced on Elysia.
issues.problem: Duplicate: this repeats almost word for word the existing Prime 3: Elysia and SkyTown line ('the Elysian Defense Drone, which with Ghor and Helios was one of Elysia's three great guardians'). It is also the Metroid Wiki 'three main bosses' meta label dressed up as in-universe fact. Elysia had other boss-level foes, including the Turbine Chamber Berserker Lord in this same batch and three Steamlords, whom Metroid Wiki lists as bosses. Ghor was a corrupted hunter, not a guardian of the planet.
issues.correction: Cut the sentence. The Elysia entry already covers it.

issues.claim: working fast because a damaged antenna regrew if the others stood too long
issues.problem: The wording is muddled. Metroid Wiki: 'After enough shots to each antenna, it will retract into the Drone's head... If Samus takes too long to shoot an antenna while another is down, the damaged antenna will return at full health.' Downed antennae retract and come back; they do not regrow.
issues.correction: ...working fast, because a downed antenna came back at full strength if she was slow to drop the next one.

issues.claim: keys: Defense Drone, Defense Drones, Ballista Storage
issues.problem: 'Defense drone' is a generic sci-fi phrase and may fire on unrelated prose. 'Ballista Storage' will also pull this entry in for the later Steamlord fight there. Both are acceptable but loose.
issues.correction: Keep as is, or add 'Elysian'/'SkyTown' as secondary keys for the bare 'Defense Drone(s)'.

result.overall: All three entries hold up on the main facts. Every logbook quote matched the full Metroid Wiki logbook text word for word: Berserker Lord, Berserker Knight, Korakk Beast, Pirate Hussar and Defense Drone. These facts are confirmed: the Docking Bay 5 Lord delayed Samus on the way to Norion (Metroid Prime 3 page). The Turbine Chamber Lord guarded the first Theronian Bomb component (Metroid Prime 3 page; a search snippet from Wikitroid agrees). Ghor's Knight kill on Norion (Ghor page and Metroid Prime 3 page) and Gandrayda's Knight form with shared weaknesses (Gandrayda page) are confirmed. Also confirmed: the Korakk's death opens the Thorn Jungle shield generator, 'one of the two generators', and the Defense Drone fight details (cage, missiles, plasma ball, shock waves, homing bombs, three antennae, Grapple Lasso, Ice Missiles and Hyper Beam, smoke). The Chozo origin of the Elysians is confirmed (Elysian and Elysia pages). No outright factual errors were found. The fixes needed: (1) Defense Drone: cut the 'Pirates never reached the room' wiki speculation. It is out of canon scope, and a Phazon-corrupted Steamlord later appears in the same room (Metroid Wiki Steamlord page and the existing Fauna of Elysia entry). Also cut the 'three great guardians' line, which repeats the Prime 3: Elysia and SkyTown entry. (2) Korakk: drop 'guards its rider with its life'. It is a wiki gloss its own citation does not support, and it clashes with the Korakk staying passive while its rider lives. Remove the irrelevant Space_Pirate_Data source. (3) Berserkers: reword the unclear 'Phazon-based attacks hurt Knights' to match the logbook's 'armor must be removed before unit can be damaged'. Optionally add the Ship Missile alternative, change 'orbs' to 'projectiles', and soften the Project Helix sentence. Keys: the bare 'Berserker(s)', 'Hussar(s)' and 'Defense Drone' are generic words that could fire on unrelated prose. None of the three duplicates an existing dedicated entry, and none contradicts the existing Norion, Olympus, Ghor, Gandrayda, Elysia, Boost Ball or fauna entries apart from the issues above. Word counts are as stated.
